chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Amr ibn Jumay', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The words of a man to a woman, "I love you," will never depart from her heart, ever.'
ai.seo_question: What is the lasting effect of saying 'I love you' to a woman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise yet profound statement from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), transmitted through a chain of reliable narrators, emphasizing the psychological permanence of verbal affection in women. This hadith is often cited by Shia scholars to highlight the importance of *kalayn al-jamil* (beautiful speech) and emotional intelligence in marital relations, suggesting that words carry a weight that actions alone may not immediately replicate. It underscores the spiritual and emotional dimensions of the husband-wife bond as a source of tranquility (*sakinah*).
